title: A Veil for the Spire
premise: Zephyrine Dravenmoor, the last swordspeaker bound by an oath she no longer understands, has spent a decade hiding among the ledgers of the Meridian Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names not yet earned. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark in a single night, she learns her guildmaster sold the covenant between realms to buy his own survival. To restore it, Zephyrine must gather a found family of debtors and defectors, confront the oath that demands her voice as payment, and choose between sealing the veil forever or leaving both realms exposed to what waits beyond. In the end she breaks her own covenant to forge a new one, paying with her swordspeech but keeping her life, her love, and a fragile sky.
about_author: Yara Okonkwo is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people trapped by their own promises. She lives between two cities and claims neither, which she insists is research.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A quiet night cataloguing impossible inventory establishes her hidden life: she speaks to blades only when alone, and never for coin. Her guildmaster, Corvane, assigns her to audit a sealed vault. The emotional beat is wary contentment—the calm of someone who believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The border wards shatter at moonrise; every star vanishes simultaneously, and the vault she audited holds a dead god's contract with Corvane's signature on it. She flees with one ledger page. The beat is vertigo—the floor of her careful life giving way.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Voices
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, intercut with letters from her late mentor. She deciphers the covenant: swordspeakers once sang the wards into being, each generation paying with part of themselves; she is the last installment. The beat is grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Debtor's Market
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Hunting allies through the Guild's black market, she recruits Sable, a thief who owes a decade of sleep, and Ilex, a disgraced warden-mason. Corvane's hunters close in. The beat is reluctant trust—found family beginning to form under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Warden Knew
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. He reveals the wards weren't broken—they were released, from inside, by someone who believed the other realm was devouring ours. Zephyrine realizes the enemy may be right. The beat is moral destabilization; duty and certainty split apart.

chapters.title: The Crossing at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The trio crosses the fallen border into the starless realm and finds not monsters but refugees—beings fleeing something worse behind them. Sable takes a wound meant for Zephyrine. The beat is compassion overriding fear; the 'enemy' becomes people.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. His history unfolds: he watched the last covenant consume his sister's voice and mind, and sold this one to end the cycle. He offers Zephyrine the same escape he took. The beat is terrible sympathy—the villain as a mirror of her own survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Oath Unbound
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered at the Spire, she must speak the old covenant or lose everything—and discovers the oath was never a chain but a door, corrupted by generations of fear-fueled amendments. The beat is revelation: the price of survival was always negotiable, if someone dared renegotiate.

chapters.title: A Veil Reforged
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, full climax. With Sable, Ilex, and even redeemed defectors, she sings a new covenant at the Spire—not a wall but a treaty, open and guarded by choice. Corvane sacrifices himself to hold the threshold while it sets. The stars return one by one. The beat is costly triumph.

chapters.title: Ledgers, Kept Differently
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue. Voiceless but whole, she reopens the Guild as a house of mediation between realms, her found family beside her, her love for Sable finally spoken in writing instead of song. The beat is quiet hope: survival was worth its price because she chose what to pay.
